subject: InfraFlow trial onboarding and integration recap
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena@infraflow.com>, Samir Patel <samir@infraflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: InfraFlow trial onboarding and integration recap

Thanks for the call this morning — good alignment and a clear path to a focused trial. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. I attached a mutual action plan and a short SDK snippet pack.

High-level objective for the 3-week trial:
- Validate retrieval + generation workflow embedded in InfraFlow's incident triage UI with under 150ms median generation latency for short completions (<=128 tokens) and acceptable token-level cost.
- Measure extraction accuracy on our labeled prompt set (provided by InfraFlow) with target F1 >= 0.82 for entity extraction tasks.
- Confirm secure routing and that no customer PII leaves their VPC during test data runs.

Success criteria (please confirm or edit):
1) End-to-end demo with sample traffic (500 sessions/day) and p95 latency < 450ms.
2) Accuracy gates: entity F1 >= 0.82; response quality pass rate >= 90% on nightly evals.
3) Ops: RBAC and audit logs enabled; SOC2 artifacts checklist reviewed.

Integration/implementation notes (technical ask):
- We propose streaming responses using our SSE-based /v1/stream endpoint for the UI to render tokens progressively. Fallback: standard /v1/generate for batch runs.
- Tool calling: InfraFlow will need a single function hook for "lookup_customer_context(customer_id)" which we can surface via our function-calling API. See sdk-route-snippets.md for example function signatures.
- Auth: short-lived tokens are recommended for the trial. We can wire up a service-account flow and rotate tokens for the sandbox.

Tentative timeline (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): final sign-off on MAP, SOC2 evidence request, and API access. (Owner: InfraFlow ops / Alex)
- Week 1: SDK integration + streaming proof-of-concept; initial QA (Owner: Karthik)
- Week 2: Run evaluation set; iterate on prompts and batching/quant profiles (Owner: Marissa)
- Week 3: Acceptance demo, performance report, and handoff to InfraFlow engineers for production checklist (Owner: Ben)

Immediate asks for InfraFlow team:
- Confirm success criteria and target traffic profile.
- Provide labeled evaluation set (S3 link or sample CSV).
- Share a preferred kickoff window for the engineering sync next Tuesday.

Attachments: infraflow-map-mutual_action_plan.xlsx, sdk-route-snippets.md, soc2-evidence-request.pdf

Thanks — I will book the kickoff once you confirm dates.

--
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Elena Ramos <elena@infraflow.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@infraflow.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: InfraFlow trial onboarding and integration recap

Thanks Alex — helpful summary. We agree with the objectives and most of the gates, with a couple of clarifications: 

- Latency target: p95 < 450ms for short completions is fine. For longer tokens (256–512) we expect p95 < 1.2s; will that be achievable with streaming + batching?
- Data residency: we need to ensure that raw logs are stored in our EU S3 buckets for regulated customer subsets. For the trial, we can keep test data in our US sandbox, but production will require EU region support.
- Tool calling: we will expose a simple HTTP endpoint for customer_context lookups. We need to see the function spec to ensure signature compatibility (we looked at sdk-route-snippets.md and the sample looks close).

Deliverables from InfraFlow this week:
- Labeled eval set (we will upload to the Drive folder you shared).
- A short doc with three production user flows to test end-to-end (we'll attach by tomorrow).

On the question of longer completions — please have Karthik call out recommended batching/quantization profile options in the kickoff so we can plan CPU/GPU footprint.

Quoted for context:
> High-level objective for the 3-week trial:
> - Validate retrieval + generation workflow embedded in InfraFlow's incident triage UI with under 150ms median generation latency for short completions (<=128 tokens) and acceptable token-level cost.

Will confirm kickoff availability after we sync internally. Thanks, Elena

--
Elena Ramos
Head of Product, InfraFlow
elena@infraflow.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena@infraflow.com>, Samir Patel <samir@infraflow.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: InfraFlow trial onboarding and integration recap

Great — adding a short implementation plan and owners so everyone has clear responsibilities before the kickoff: 

Implementation tasks (initial owners):
- API access and Service Account setup: Alex to provision trial credentials and a short-lived token flow. (Alex)
- SDK integration (React UI + mobile shim): Karthik to deliver a small demo repo showing streaming hook and function-call wiring. (Karthik)
- Prompt set & eval harness: Marissa will ingest InfraFlow's labeled set into our nightly eval runner and prepare an initial accuracy report by end of Week 1. (Marissa)
- Batching + quantization recommendations: Karthik to propose two config profiles (low-latency & cost-optimized) and expected metrics.
- SOC2 evidence checklist & compliance handoff: Ben to coordinate and track documentation with InfraFlow's security contact.

Technical checklist (short):
- Streaming: /v1/stream SSE — front-end subscribes to token frames; include incremental metadata frames with {cursor_position, partial_score}.
- Fallback: /v1/generate (POST) for batch evaluation runs; use chunked uploads for large eval files.
- Function calling: call name "lookup_customer_context" with schema: {customer_id: string, include_recent_incidents: boolean}. Redwood will sign requests to the function gateway and replay authorization via InfraFlow service token.
- Rate limiting for trial: default 50 QPS, bumpable to 200 QPS with prior notice.

Kickoff agenda (30–45m):
1) Quick intros and success criteria review (5m)
2) SDK demo: streaming + function call example (10–15m)
3) Auth and sandbox access walkthrough (5–10m)
4) Q&A and next steps / timeline confirmation (10m)

I will schedule the kickoff for Tuesday at 11:00 PT if InfraFlow confirms — otherwise propose two alternate windows in the doc.

Quoted from Elena for reference:
> Data residency: we need to ensure that raw logs are stored in our EU S3 buckets for regulated customer subsets. For the trial, we can keep test data in our US sandbox, but production will require EU region support.

Open items for the kickoff:
- Karthik: share streaming demo repo before the call (link in Drive).
- Alex: provision service account + pre-seed test token.
- InfraFlow: drop labeled eval set and 3 user flows in Drive.

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

From: Samir Patel <samir@infraflow.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena@infraflow.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: InfraFlow trial onboarding and integration recap

Thanks everyone — this looks good. We confirmed internally and can meet for the engineering kickoff on Tuesday at 11:00 PT. A couple quick clarifications before the call: 

- We'll upload the labeled set to the Drive folder today (InfraFlow-Private/labeled_eval.csv).
- For the EU production requirement: trial is fine in US sandbox; however please note our security team will want to see the SOC2 evidence request PDF prior to moving to production. Samir (ops) will be on the kickoff to validate the checklist.
- On function calling — we prefer synchronous HTTP calls (200ms target) for the lookup; if your function gateway introduces >300ms added latency we'll need to consider a local cache.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

--
Samir Patel
Director, Platform Engineering, InfraFlow
samir@infraflow.com
